progress.checking: Watch the shutter: Home Assistant moves it up, then down, briefly.
progress.pairing:
You have {seconds} seconds to perform this sequence on the shutter's original remote:

1. Press up, and wait for the shutter to reach the top.
2. Press down, and let about four slats appear.
3. Press stop.
4. Press up again, and wait for the top.

Then leave the shutter alone until the time is up. Home Assistant then moves it up, then down, briefly, to check the pairing.
progress.unpairing:
You have {seconds} seconds to perform this sequence on the shutter's original remote:

1. Press down, and wait for the shutter to reach the bottom.
2. Press up, and let about two slats appear.
3. Press stop.
4. Press down again, and wait for the bottom.

The shutter should answer with a short back-and-forth. Then leave it alone until the time is up. Home Assistant then moves it up, then down, briefly, to check the unpairing.

data_description.shutter: The shutter to remove from Home Assistant.

forget.description:
**This does not unpair the shutter.** It only removes it from Home Assistant, for a shutter that no longer obeys its channel, such as one whose motor was replaced. A shutter that still obeys has to be unpaired instead.

Once you submit, Home Assistant moves the shutter up, then down, briefly, and only forgets it if it does not move.
forget.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::forget%]

forget_check.description: Home Assistant just moved the shutter up, then down, briefly. If it did not move, no shutter obeys the channel any more, and it can be forgotten. If it moved, it still obeys: unpair it instead.
forget_check.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::forget%]

pair.description:
Pairing is done from the shutter's own remote. The dongle only opens a window for it, and only the shutter you drive during that window is paired — the others are left alone.

Before you continue, move the shutter to mid-travel and keep its original remote at hand.

Once you submit, you have {seconds} seconds to:

1. Press up, and wait for the shutter to reach the top.
2. Press down, and let about four slats appear.
3. Press stop.
4. Press up again, and wait for the top.

Then leave the shutter alone until the time is up. Home Assistant then moves it up, then down, briefly, and asks you whether it moved.
pair.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::pair%]

pair_check.description: Home Assistant just moved the shutter up, then down, briefly, on its new channel. If it moved, it is paired. If it did not, the pairing did not take.
pair_check.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::pair%]

data_description.shutter: The shutter that should stop obeying Home Assistant. It keeps answering its original remote.

unpair.description:
Unpairing is done from the shutter's own remote. The dongle only opens a window for it, and only the shutter you drive during that window is unpaired — the others are left alone.

Before you continue, move the shutter to mid-travel and keep its original remote at hand.

Once you submit, you have {seconds} seconds to:

1. Press down, and wait for the shutter to reach the bottom.
2. Press up, and let about two slats appear.
3. Press stop.
4. Press down again, and wait for the bottom.

The shutter should answer with a short back-and-forth. Then leave it alone until the time is up. Home Assistant then moves it up, then down, briefly, and asks you whether it moved.
unpair.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::unpair%]

unpair_check.description: Home Assistant just moved the shutter up, then down, briefly, on the channel being unpaired. If it did not move, it is unpaired. If it moved, it still obeys the channel.
unpair_check.title: [%key:component::neosol::options::step::init::menu_options::unpair%]
